about: Curated list of real US colleges for Groundwork's College interview track. Every fact comes from the school's own website (see each entry's sources). Interview policies change every year: re-check before relying on them.

fields.size: Small = under 5,000 undergraduates, Medium = 5,000-15,000, Large = over 15,000
fields.region: Northeast | Mid-Atlantic | South | Midwest | Southwest | West
fields.interview.type: alumni | admissions | both | none (none = the school doesn't offer evaluative interviews; Groundwork labels it 'Practice only')
fields.interview.status: short plain description from the official page
fields.selectivity: 1 = most selective (Ivy or near-Ivy, admits roughly under 10%), 2 = roughly 10-20%, 3 = roughly 20-40%, 4 = roughly 40-65%, 5 = over roughly 65%. APPROXIMATE bands based on recently published admission rates, not official figures; used only to give each student a spread from reach to more accessible schools.
fields.founded, research, affiliation, athletic: From a reference file compiled 2026-09-29 (Wikipedia infoboxes, the 2025 Carnegie research list, and official university and athletics sites). research is the 2025 Carnegie designation (R1 or R2). Athletics conferences change often; re-check yearly.
fields.facts, about, strengths (schools added 2: Built only from the reference fields above; interview details come from each school's official admissions page (first URL in sources).

schools.name: Tufts University
strengths: Research university with a liberal arts feel
facts: Every first-year lights a candle on the President's Lawn on their first night, to honor Charles Tufts
Tuftonia's Day celebrates the university's birthday with a campus carnival at the end of spring semester
Students paint the Medford Cannon and guard it until dawn so no one paints over their design
schools.about: Tufts is a research university on a hilltop just outside Boston, about a mile from Davis Square in Somerville. It has about 6,900 undergraduates and dates back to 1852.

interview.status: Optional alumni interview for first-year applicants; you opt in on the Common App. Usually held in a public place like a coffee shop or library.

knownFor: Fletcher School of Law and Diplomacy

schools.name: Bowdoin College
strengths: Strong ties to the state of Maine
facts: A lobster bake welcomes students each fall, and seniors share another the night before Commencement
Saying a friendly hello to people on campus is a tradition that dates back to the 1960s
Ivies is the spring celebration that marks the end of the long Maine winter
schools.about: Bowdoin is a small liberal arts college in the town of Brunswick, Maine, chartered in 1794. It's known for a close-knit community and a strong connection to Maine.

interview.status: Interviews strongly encouraged but not required. Offered in person or virtually with admissions staff, students, or alumni.

schools.name: Middlebury College
facts: Students take one intensive course during January, called J-Term
February graduates ski down the Middlebury Snow Bowl in caps and gowns
Its Winter Carnival, started in 1923, is the oldest student-run carnival in the country
schools.about: Middlebury is a small liberal arts college in central Vermont, between the Green Mountains and the Adirondacks. It's nationally known for environmental studies and international studies.

interview.status: Optional alumni interview by video or phone; request it in your applicant portal after applying. Not guaranteed, and no on-campus interviews.

knownFor: Environmental studies (first undergraduate program in the US)
Middlebury Institute of International Studies at Monterey

schools.name: Wesleyan University
facts: Its open curriculum has no required core; you build your own plan with your advisor each semester
You can combine majors, minors and certificates in your own mix
Wesleyan has been in Middletown, Connecticut since 1831
schools.about: Wesleyan is a liberal arts university of about 2,900 undergraduates in the small city of Middletown, Connecticut. It's known for its open curriculum, where you design your own path.

interview.status: No evaluative interview. Optional WesChats with current students are informal and not part of your application.

schools.name: Brown University
facts: The Open Curriculum, adopted in 1969, has no general education requirements
Students choose a 'concentration' instead of a major
The campus sits on College Hill, overlooking downtown Providence
schools.about: Brown is a research university in Providence, Rhode Island, with about 7,300 undergraduates. Its Open Curriculum lets students design their own education.

interview.status: No interviews since 2019-20. Brown instead invites an optional short video introduction.

schools.name: Dartmouth College
strengths: Liberal arts focus at a research university
facts: The D-Plan quarter system includes 'sophomore summer' on campus
First-years start with an outdoor orientation trip led by returning students
Winter Carnival has been held for over 100 years, with a bonfire on the Green
schools.about: Dartmouth is a small research university in Hanover, New Hampshire, on the Connecticut River, founded in 1769. It has about 4,300 undergraduates and a strong liberal arts focus.

interview.status: Optional alumni interview, in person or virtual. Alumni contact you after you apply; not everyone can be offered one.

schools.name: Williams College
facts: On Mountain Day each fall, classes are canceled so everyone can hike, with cider donuts and a picnic
Mountain Day traces back to 'Chip Day' and 'Gravel Day' holidays from around 1800
About 2,100 students learn closely alongside faculty
schools.about: Williams is a small liberal arts college of about 2,100 students in Williamstown, Massachusetts, in the mountains of the Berkshires. It's known for close relationships between students and faculty.

interview.status: No evaluative interviews. Seniors can request an optional, non-evaluative conversation with an admission officer or alum that doesn't affect decisions.

schools.name: Smith College
strengths: Over 1,000 courses in 83 areas of study
facts: Smith's only required course is a writing-intensive class in your first year
In 2004 it graduated the first engineers from a U.S. women's college
The 147-acre campus sits in the lively small city of Northampton
schools.about: Smith is a women's liberal arts college of about 2,500 students in Northampton, Massachusetts. Its open curriculum lets you mix subjects freely, and it was the first U.S. women's college to graduate engineers.

interview.status: Optional interview for first-year applicants, usually with an alum volunteer; admission counselors and student interviewers also interview. Request it through your applicant portal.

schools.name: Wellesley College
facts: Seniors in graduation robes race wooden hoops down Tupelo Lane; the winner gets tossed into Lake Waban
On a surprise Lake Day each fall, classes are canceled for carnival rides and games
Every sophomore class since 1879 has planted a tree
schools.about: Wellesley is a women's liberal arts college of just under 2,300 students, 12 miles west of Boston. It's known for traditions like hooprolling and Lake Day.

interview.status: Wellesley does not offer interviews as part of the admission process.

schools.name: Northeastern University
facts: Students alternate classes with full-time co-op jobs, usually about six months long
You can do up to two co-ops in four years, and you don't pay tuition while on co-op
Co-ops happen around Boston and around the world
schools.about: Northeastern is a research university in the middle of Boston. It's built around co-op, where students alternate semesters of classes with full-time jobs related to their studies.

interview.status: No alumni or on-campus interviews. Northeastern will consider third-party video interviews (InitialView, Vericant).

athletics.conference: Coastal Athletic Association (CAA); ice hockey: Hockey East

schools.name: Boston University
facts: Commonwealth Avenue runs right through the Charles River Campus, with a Green Line stop
New first-years spend a day volunteering around Boston before classes start
BU was the first coeducational college in Massachusetts
schools.about: Boston University is a large private research university in the heart of Boston, with more than 37,000 students in total. Its main campus stretches along Commonwealth Avenue by the Charles River.

interview.status: Interviews aren't required and aren't offered for most first-year applicants (except some special programs like accelerated medical/dental and theatre).

athletics.conference: Patriot League; ice hockey: Hockey East

schools.name: Worcester Polytechnic Institute
facts: The year is split into seven-week terms, with three courses at a time
About 85 percent of undergraduates travel off campus for at least one project
First-years start with the Great Problems Seminar
schools.about: WPI is a tech-focused university in Worcester, Massachusetts, known for project-based learning. Students work on real team projects at 50+ project centers on six continents.

interview.status: WPI doesn't offer admission interviews; you can book a one-on-one meeting with a counselor instead.

schools.name: Olin College of Engineering
facts: Finalists are invited to Candidates' Weekend, which includes a student-run Design Challenge
Olin evaluates teamwork, communication and collaboration, not tricky technical puzzles
It's one of the only colleges that uses a Candidates' Weekend in admissions
schools.about: Olin is a very small engineering college outside Boston built around hands-on, team-based projects. Finalists visit for Candidates' Weekend, with an interview and a group exercise.

interview.status: Invited finalists must attend Candidates' Weekend, which includes an evaluated individual interview and group exercise (virtual for students outside the continental U.S.).

schools.name: University of Vermont
facts: UVM stands for Universitas Viridis Montis, Latin for 'University of the Green Mountains'
Chartered in 1791, it was the fifth college in New England
The campus looks out over Lake Champlain and the Adirondack Mountains
schools.about: The University of Vermont is a public university of about 11,600 undergraduates in Burlington, Vermont's largest city, next to Lake Champlain. It's known for its focus on the environment and health.

interview.status: Interviews aren't part of UVM's first-year application steps; you can book a video chat with an admissions counselor to ask questions.

athletics.conference: America East Conference; ice hockey: Hockey East

knownFor: Rubenstein School of Environment and Natural Resources

schools.name: Rhode Island School of Design
facts: All first-years take the same studio program, Experimental and Foundation Studies: drawing, design and spatial dynamics
A five-year dual degree with Brown gives you a RISD BFA plus a Brown bachelor's
You apply with a portfolio of 12–20 recent pieces
schools.about: RISD is an art and design school in Providence, Rhode Island, next door to Brown. Every first-year starts with the same foundation studio year before choosing a major.

interview.status: No admission interviews; RISD offers portfolio reviews and info sessions instead. A portfolio is part of the application.

schools.name: Columbia University
facts: Every Columbia College student takes the Core Curriculum, created in 1919
Frontiers of Science became part of the Core in 2004
The main campus is in Morningside Heights in Manhattan
schools.about: Columbia is a research university in New York City's Morningside Heights. Undergraduates in Columbia College share the Core Curriculum, small seminars on great works that date back to 1919.

interview.status: Alumni interviews were discontinued starting fall 2023; interviews are not part of the application.

knownFor: School of International and Public Affairs
Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons

schools.name: Cornell University
strengths: Wide range of colleges and majors
facts: Founded on the idea of 'an institution where any person can find instruction in any study'
On Dragon Day, first-year architecture students parade a giant dragon that battles an engineering phoenix
Slope Day celebrates the last day of classes on Libe Slope
schools.about: Cornell is a large research university in Ithaca, New York, founded in 1865. It has more than 1,000 student organizations and famous traditions like Dragon Day and Slope Day.

interview.status: Cornell doesn't offer true interviews (except Architecture, which requires a video interview). Optional alumni 'contact meetings' are informal and not interviews.

knownFor: College of Agriculture and Life Sciences

schools.name: Vassar College
strengths: A pioneer in women's education, coeducational since 1969
facts: Founder's Day, first held in 1866 as a surprise birthday party for Matthew Vassar, now ends with carnival rides and fireworks
Vassar was founded in 1861 as a pioneer in women's education
Poughkeepsie is a small city on the Hudson River, about 75 miles north of New York City
schools.about: Vassar is a liberal arts college of about 2,450 students in Poughkeepsie, New York, on the Hudson River. It was founded in 1861 for women and has been coeducational since 1969.

interview.status: Optional alumni interviews for domestic first-year applicants after you apply. They're informational, not evaluative, and not everyone can get one.

schools.name: Hamilton College
facts: There are no distribution requirements, but you take three writing-intensive courses
About 15 percent of students are the first in their family to attend college
The 1,350-acre hilltop campus dates back to 1793
schools.about: Hamilton is a liberal arts college of about 1,850 students on a hilltop in Clinton, New York. It has an open curriculum and a strong focus on clear writing and speaking.

interview.status: Interviews strongly encouraged. Mostly by video, some on campus in fall, with admission officers or trained Hamilton seniors.

schools.name: University of Pennsylvania
strengths: Four undergraduate schools: Arts & Sciences, Engineering, Nursing and Wharton (business)
Combining liberal arts with professional schools
facts: Penn calls itself America's first university, with a history dating to 1740
On Hey Day, juniors parade across campus in straw hats and red T-shirts, carrying canes, to become seniors
Undergraduates can take classes across all four undergraduate schools
schools.about: Penn is a research university in Philadelphia with four undergraduate schools, including Wharton and Nursing. Its history dates to 1740.

interview.status: Penn no longer offers alumni conversations as part of the application process.

knownFor: School of Engineering and Applied Science

schools.name: Princeton University
strengths: Senior thesis with a faculty adviser
Undergraduate focus at a research university
facts: Every senior writes a thesis or does a major independent project, one-on-one with a professor
First-years are randomly placed in one of seven residential colleges
New students are welcomed in the Pre-rade by running through FitzRandolph Gate
schools.about: Princeton is a research university of about 5,200 undergraduates in Princeton, New Jersey. Every senior works one-on-one with a professor on a thesis, and students live in residential colleges.

interview.status: Optional alumni interview after you apply (you can opt out). 30–45 minute informal conversation; not guaranteed everywhere.

knownFor: School of Engineering and Applied Science
School of Public and International Affairs

schools.name: Swarthmore College
strengths: Engineering at a liberal arts college
facts: In the Honors Program, outside experts travel to campus to give students oral exams
It's one of few liberal arts colleges with an undergraduate engineering program
The 425-acre campus is the Scott Arboretum, with over 4,000 kinds of plants
schools.about: Swarthmore is a liberal arts college of about 1,640 students outside Philadelphia. Its campus is an arboretum, and it offers engineering alongside the liberal arts.

interview.status: Optional virtual or in-person interviews for U.S. first-year applicants with a current student (Admissions Fellow) or an alum. No disadvantage if you don't interview.

knownFor: Engineering (rare at a liberal arts college)
Tri-College Consortium (with Bryn Mawr and Haverford)

schools.name: Haverford College
strengths: Classes with nearby Bryn Mawr College
facts: The Honor Code, in place since 1896, is written and governed entirely by students
Students serve on hiring committees and run more than 140 clubs
Haverford has Quaker roots that shape its values of equality and community
schools.about: Haverford is a liberal arts college outside Philadelphia on an arboretum campus. It's known for academic rigor and an Honor Code run entirely by students.

interview.status: Interviews recommended but not required. All by Zoom, with admission staff, senior interviewers, or alumni; all valued equally.

schools.name: Bryn Mawr College
strengths: Graduate school alongside the college since 1885
facts: At Lantern Night, each first-year receives a lantern in their class color to 'light her way through college'
Grand May Day, held every four years since 1900, fills the day with dancing, plays and concerts
Major traditions end with the whole community singing together at Step Sing
schools.about: Bryn Mawr is a women's liberal arts college outside Philadelphia, founded in 1885. It's known for traditions like Lantern Night and May Day.

interview.status: Not required but strongly encouraged. On campus or on Zoom, with admissions or alumnae interviewers; you can interview once.

schools.name: Carnegie Mellon University
facts: Buggy, a 100-year-old race of engine-free vehicles around Schenley Park, is the highlight of Spring Carnival
Buggies can hit about 35 mph and are designed and built by student teams
Spring Carnival has been held in some form for more than 100 years
schools.about: Carnegie Mellon is a research university in Pittsburgh known for computer science, engineering and the arts. Its Spring Carnival features Buggy, a student-built race that's over 100 years old.

interview.status: No interviews for most applicants (Architecture uses Zoom interviews; Drama uses auditions and portfolios).

athletics.conference: University Athletic Association (UAA); football: Centennial Conference

schools.name: Penn State University Park
facts: THON is a 46-hour, student-run dance marathon that has raised over $200 million for kids with cancer
The Berkey Creamery is the largest university creamery in the U.S.
Penn State was founded as an agricultural college
schools.about: Penn State's main campus is a large public university in State College, Pennsylvania. It's famous for THON, a huge student-run charity dance marathon, and its campus ice cream.

interview.status: Interviews aren't typically part of first-year admission (only some special programs and arts majors).

schools.name: Johns Hopkins University
facts: About 70 percent of undergraduates do research outside their classes
Hopkins was the nation's first research university
The Homewood campus has red-brick buildings and green quads in North Baltimore
schools.about: Johns Hopkins is a research university in Baltimore where about 5,000 undergraduates study on the Homewood campus. Most undergraduates take part in research.

interview.status: Johns Hopkins doesn't offer interviews in undergraduate admissions.

schools.name: Georgetown University
strengths: International affairs (Walsh School of Foreign Service)
facts: It's the oldest Catholic and Jesuit university in the U.S., founded in 1789
The School of Foreign Service, founded in 1919, is the oldest school of international affairs in the U.S.
Students intern near the State Department, World Bank and think tanks
schools.about: Georgetown is a Jesuit university in Washington, DC, founded in 1789. It's known for international affairs and public service.

interview.status: Alumni interview required for all first-year applicants (waived only where no alumni are available). You arrange it after applying.

athletics.conference: Big East Conference; football: Patriot League

schools.name: Howard University
strengths: The only HBCU with an R1 research designation
Fine arts (Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts)
facts: Howard's first Homecoming game, in 1924, helped start a national tradition
Homecoming draws more than 100,000 people each fall
Yardfest brings major music artists to campus
schools.about: Howard is a historically Black research university in Washington, DC, founded in 1867. Its Homecoming is one of the biggest celebrations in college life.

interview.status: Interviews aren't part of general first-year admission (music and acting programs use auditions with interviews).

schools.name: University of Maryland
strengths: Living-learning programs (College Park Scholars, Honors College)
facts: Students rub the nose of the Testudo terrapin statue for good luck, especially at finals
College Park Scholars offers 13 themed two-year living-learning programs
UMD was founded in 1856
schools.about: The University of Maryland is a large public research university in College Park, near Washington, DC, with 31,000+ undergraduates. Many first-years join themed living-learning programs.

interview.status: Interviews aren't listed as part of the first-year application.

knownFor: A. James Clark School of Engineering
Robert H. Smith School of Business

schools.name: Duke University
facts: All first-years live together on East Campus, then move to West Campus in the 'Bricks to Stone' tradition
Students camp in tents for weeks in Krzyzewskiville to get seats at big basketball games
Duke Chapel's 210-foot tower holds a 50-bell carillon; its chief designer, Julian Abele, was America's first Black architect of renown
schools.about: Duke is a research university in Durham, North Carolina, with a Gothic West Campus centered on Duke Chapel. First-years all live together on East Campus.

interview.status: Optional alumni interview by video or phone after you apply. Duke can't interview everyone and prioritizes some applicants.

schools.name: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
strengths: The oldest public university in the U.S.
facts: On the first day of classes, students take a 'First Sip' from the Old Well for good luck
UNC was chartered in 1789, making it the nation's oldest public university
Its debate societies, founded in 1795, are the oldest student groups on campus
schools.about: UNC–Chapel Hill is the oldest public university in the country, in the college town of Chapel Hill, North Carolina. The Old Well is its best-known symbol.

interview.status: UNC does not use interviews in its admissions review.

knownFor: Gillings School of Global Public Health
Hussman School of Journalism and Media

schools.name: Davidson College
facts: Thanks to the Honor Code, final exams are unproctored and self-scheduled
The night before exams, students gather for the Midnight Scream
Faculty and staff serve students a late-night breakfast during finals week
schools.about: Davidson is a liberal arts college near Charlotte, North Carolina, with a student-run Honor Code that dates to its founding in 1837. Students schedule their own unproctored final exams.

interview.status: Davidson doesn't offer evaluative interviews; you can chat informally with current students instead.

athletics.conference: Atlantic 10 Conference (A-10); football: Pioneer Football League

schools.name: Wake Forest University
strengths: Small classes at a university (10:1 student-faculty ratio)
facts: After big wins, students 'roll the Quad' by covering the center of campus with toilet paper streamers
More than half of undergraduate classes have fewer than 20 students
Project Pumpkin brings local kids to campus for a student-run fall festival
schools.about: Wake Forest is a university of about 5,500 undergraduates in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, with small classes and a liberal arts focus. It's famous for rolling the Quad after big wins.

interview.status: Optional 20–30 minute Zoom interview with an admissions representative for seniors who've applied; request within five days of applying. Not everyone can be accommodated.

schools.name: Emory University
strengths: Liberal arts at a research university
Two starting points: the Atlanta campus or Oxford College
facts: You can start at the Atlanta campus or spend two years at the small Oxford College campus 38 miles away
Dooley, a skeleton called the 'Lord of Misrule', is Emory's unofficial mascot
During Dooley's Week, Dooley interrupts classes and pops up around campus
schools.about: Emory is a research university in Atlanta with a strong liberal arts focus. Students can begin at the Atlanta campus or at Oxford College, a small campus nearby.

interview.status: No interviews with admission staff. A small number of first-year applicants in certain cities may be invited to an alumni interview.

knownFor: Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing

schools.name: Spelman College
strengths: Education of women of African descent
facts: Students wear white dresses for formal ceremonies, a tradition dating to 1900
Each class receives its own emblem and colors, passed down since 1927
Students can cross-register at Morehouse and Clark Atlanta and share the Woodruff Library
schools.about: Spelman is a historically Black liberal arts college for women in Atlanta, founded in 1881, with more than 2,700 students. It's part of the Atlanta University Center with Morehouse and Clark Atlanta.

interview.status: Interviews aren't mentioned in Spelman's first-year application requirements or FAQ.

knownFor: Spelman College Museum of Fine Art

schools.name: Morehouse College
strengths: #1 producer of Black men who earn doctorates
Most Rhodes Scholars of any HBCU
facts: Morehouse is the nation's only historically Black private liberal arts college for men
Crown Forum is a required community gathering that dates back to the college's early years
Becoming a 'Morehouse Man' centers on service and social responsibility
schools.about: Morehouse is a historically Black liberal arts college for men in Atlanta, founded in 1867, with more than 2,200 students. It's known for producing leaders and scholars.

interview.status: Not a standard step, but Morehouse says applicants may be invited to interview during the review process. Confirm details with admissions.

schools.name: Georgia Institute of Technology
strengths: Public tech university in a big city
facts: The Ramblin' Wreck, a 1930 Ford Model A, leads the football team onto the field
Students build their own contraptions for the Ramblin' Wreck Parade, held since 1932
Students call themselves Ramblin' Wrecks
schools.about: Georgia Tech is a public technology university in the middle of Atlanta, known for engineering and computing. Its mascot is a vintage car called the Ramblin' Wreck.

interview.status: Interviews are not part of admission at Georgia Tech (no alumni or staff interviews).

schools.name: Vanderbilt University
facts: All first-years live on The Martha Rivers Ingram Commons in one of 10 houses, each with a faculty head
The Commons Ball each February transforms the Commons Center for a themed dance
Nashville has more than 20,000 live music performances a year
schools.about: Vanderbilt is a research university of about 6,900 undergraduates in the middle of Nashville. All first-years live together on The Ingram Commons.

interview.status: Vanderbilt doesn't offer interviews through admissions; optional video submissions via Glimpse or InitialView instead.

schools.name: Rice University
facts: Every student is randomly assigned to one of 11 residential colleges for all four years
Beer Bike, dating to 1957, is a relay race between the colleges (water for those under 21)
Rice has no fraternities or sororities
schools.about: Rice is a research university in Houston where every student belongs to one of 11 residential colleges. Traditions like Beer Bike bring the colleges together.

interview.status: Recommended but optional and not guaranteed. Virtual interviews with a Rice alum or current student after you apply.

schools.name: Tulane University
facts: Tulane was the first private research university to require public service to graduate
First-years take a TIDES course that explores a niche interest and New Orleans
CACTUS, founded in 1966, is one of the oldest student-run volunteer groups in the country
schools.about: Tulane is a research university of about 8,200 undergraduates in New Orleans. Every student does public service as part of graduating.

interview.status: Optional interviews and coffee chats; not interviewing won't hurt your chances.

knownFor: Celia Scott Weatherhead School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine

schools.name: University of Virginia
strengths: Jefferson's Academical Village (a UNESCO World Heritage site)
facts: Top fourth-years are chosen by their peers to live in rooms on the historic Lawn
The student-run Honor System dates to 1842; new students sign the Honor Code at Convocation
The Lawn hosts traditions like Lighting of the Lawn and Rotunda Sing
schools.about: UVA is a public university in Charlottesville, Virginia, founded by Thomas Jefferson. Its original Academical Village is a UNESCO World Heritage site, and students run its Honor System.

interview.status: UVA does not offer interviews for undergraduate admission.

schools.name: William & Mary
strengths: Public university with a liberal arts feel
facts: At the Yule Log ceremony, students toss holly into the fire in the Wren Building's Great Hall for good luck
The Yule Log tradition began in 1930
Students decorate the Wren portico trees with paper doves carrying messages of gratitude
schools.about: William & Mary is a public university in historic Williamsburg, Virginia, with a small-college feel. Its Wren Building is the heart of traditions like the Yule Log ceremony.

interview.status: Optional 20–30 minute interviews with trained W&M seniors, in summer for rising seniors and fall for seniors. Fewer than 20% of applicants interview; no disadvantage if you don't.

athletics.conference: Coastal Athletic Association (CAA); football: Patriot League (from 2026)

knownFor: Raymond A. Mason School of Business
Undergraduate research in the liberal arts

schools.name: Hampton University
strengths: Waterfront campus on the Chesapeake Bay
facts: The Emancipation Oak was the site of the first Southern reading of the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863
National Geographic named the Emancipation Oak one of the 10 Great Trees of the World
Booker T. Washington graduated from Hampton and went on to help found Tuskegee
schools.about: Hampton is a historically Black university founded in 1868, on the waterfront near the mouth of the Chesapeake Bay in Virginia. Its Emancipation Oak is a landmark of American history.

interview.status: Interviews aren't listed in Hampton's freshman application requirements.

schools.name: Xavier University of Louisiana
facts: Xavier is the only historically Black Catholic university in the U.S.
It's a national leader in sending Black students to medical school
Its College of Pharmacy is one of the top producers of Black pharmacists
schools.about: Xavier is a historically Black Catholic university in New Orleans, founded in 1915. It's known nationally for preparing students for medicine and pharmacy.

interview.status: Interviews aren't part of Xavier's general freshman application (the College of Pharmacy has its own process).

schools.name: Florida A&M University
facts: The Marching 100 band has been refined for over a century
FAMU's pharmacy program is the only one in the U.S. with a fully accredited Institute of Public Health
FAMU enrolls nearly 10,000 students from across the U.S. and 70+ countries
schools.about: FAMU is a public, historically Black university in Tallahassee, Florida, with nearly 10,000 students. It's famous for the Marching 100 and its pharmacy program.

interview.status: Interviews aren't a general freshman requirement (some programs, like the College of Education, have their own interview).

schools.name: University of Florida
facts: Gator Growl, started in 1923, is the nation's largest student-run pep rally
The football stadium is nicknamed 'The Swamp'
There are more Gator statues on campus than statues of people in Gainesville
schools.about: The University of Florida is a large public research university in Gainesville. It's known for huge school spirit, from the Gator Chomp to Gator Growl.

interview.status: Interviews aren't part of standard freshman admission (the School of Music requires one).

knownFor: Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (IFAS)

schools.name: Berea College
strengths: Work program: every student has a campus job
facts: Berea hasn't charged tuition since 1892
Every student works at least 10 hours a week in one of 100+ campus job programs
Founded in 1855 by abolitionists, it was the first interracial and coeducational college in the South
schools.about: Berea is a tuition-free liberal arts college in Kentucky for promising students with limited financial resources, especially from Appalachia. Every student works a campus job.

interview.status: Not a formal interview, but conversations with an Admissions Specialist are part of how Berea evaluates applicants.

schools.name: Sewanee: The University of the South
facts: The 13,000-acre Domain has trails, bluffs, caves and a 19-mile Perimeter Trail
Students with academic distinction wear academic gowns to class as members of the Order of the Gown
Drivers tap their car roof to collect their 'Sewanee angel' as they pass through the gates
schools.about: Sewanee is a small liberal arts university on a 13,000-acre mountain campus in Tennessee called the Domain. It's known for traditions like the Order of the Gown.

interview.status: Optional 20–25 minute conversations with admission counselors (not offered November–early March), plus non-evaluative interviews with trained seniors.

schools.name: University of Chicago
facts: Scav Hunt, started in 1987, is a four-day scavenger hunt where teams build, perform and solve hundreds of odd items
Scav teams once built a working nuclear reactor in a dorm, in 1999
The campus is in the Hyde Park neighborhood of Chicago
